Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

She will be there from October sixth through October twenty-second, and the connection drops whenever the weather turns, so the app needs to keep working without a network. This is a request for a setup plan, not a request to buy devices. Mara already has a small tablet, a phone, and a borrowed e-ink reader. The tablet is the one she uses for notes, the phone is for checking maps, and the e-ink reader is for long chapters. The three devices have different storage limits, so please do not assume that a file copied to one is also present on the others.

Mara has eighteen books in the current reading list, and four are reference manuals with diagrams. She needs those four manuals available on the tablet because she marks them up there. The other fourteen books are novels and essays, and should be available on the e-ink reader as well as the tablet. The phone only needs the first three novels because Mara reads them while she waits for the ferry. Please leave the map files in the phone documents folder and do not include them in the reading list. The app currently shows all eighteen titles, but two have duplicate covers. One says “Glass Harbor Revised,” and the other says “Glass Harbor Final.” She asked me to keep both entries visible until she confirms which edition she wants.

For the local library, use the folder named Island Shelf inside the app data directory, and make that folder the first location the app checks when it opens a book. Please do not move the original EPUB files out of Mara’s existing archive folder because her notes program links to that location. The archive has a mix of EPUB and PDF files, and the manuals are PDF. The novels are EPUB. Keep their current filenames so Mara can match them with a paper checklist. The checklist has a blue mark beside manuals and a pencil mark beside books she has already finished. There are five finished books, and they should remain in the library but not appear in the Continue Reading row.

Please turn on the setting named reader.prefer_local and make the app choose the local copy before it tries to open a cloud copy if both are present. The setting should not delete a cloud copy, and it should not change the sync schedule. I almost said, “Turn off cloud sync,” but no, leave cloud sync on because Mara wants new notes copied to her home computer when she gets a connection again. The last successful sync was on September twenty-ninth, and that date is only a reference for her, not a deadline. The app should not try to upload anything while the station has no connection.
reader.prefer_local

There is a numbered section for the behavior she wants when she opens a title:
1. If a local copy is present, open that copy and show the last page she read.
2. If there is no local copy, show the title in the library and offer a download when a connection is available, but do not start a download on its own.
3. If both copies are present, keep using the local copy and leave the cloud copy untouched.

The second item matters because the station uses a metered satellite link, and Mara wants to decide which books use it. She has a daily allowance of two hundred megabytes for all personal browsing, and the app must not treat that amount as a download target or a promise that the link will be available.

On the e-ink reader, the text size is currently set to seventeen, and Mara asked to keep it at seventeen because she reads without her glasses in the evening. Set the line spacing to one point four, and leave the margin setting at medium. Those values apply only to the e-ink reader. On the tablet, keep the text size at sixteen. The tablet is used at the desk, and the bigger type makes the diagrams harder to see. Do not copy the e-ink reader display settings over to the tablet. The phone can keep its current text size, which Mara does not know by memory.

Mara told me, “I want to open a book on the island and not have to guess whether it is saved here.” She also said, “If the app cannot find a local file, tell me what is missing but wait for me before using the satellite connection.” That condition still applies if the title is one of the first three novels listed for the phone. The phone can show a download option, but it must wait for Mara to choose it. If the file is already local, then open it without asking her to choose between the local and cloud versions.

Please put a small status label beside each title that says “On device” when a local copy is available and “Not downloaded” when it is not available locally. The label should reflect the device Mara is looking at rather than the whole account. If a title is on the tablet but not on the e-ink reader, the e-ink reader should still show “Not downloaded.” Keep the two Glass Harbor entries separate for now, and do not rename either title. The app can display the file type in the details panel because the PDF manuals need to be easy to distinguish from the EPUB books, but the type label should not replace the title.

The station tablet has thirty-two gigabytes of storage with eleven gigabytes free today, and Mara wants to reserve at least three gigabytes for field notes and photographs. Do not calculate a number of books that fit because the PDF sizes are not all the same. Instead, show her the size of each selected download before she confirms it. The e-ink reader has eight gigabytes total and two gigabytes free, and it already contains audio files that should not be removed. The phone has sixty-four gigabytes total and twenty gigabytes free, but its available space changes when map packages are refreshed.

At home, Mara uses a laptop running the same reading app, and she wants its library left as it is. She asked only about the three island devices. Do not change the laptop settings or remove any reading history from the account. When she returns to the station office on October twenty-third, she may reconnect the devices and review the duplicate edition then. Until she confirms it, the app should keep both titles and their separate reading positions. If one device cannot complete a local copy before the trip, show which title still needs attention and leave its original archive file in place."}]
